label: Person
name: Ad Abi Karam
summary:
Ad Abi Karam (b. 1944) is a retired Lebanese-Australian Maronite Catholic bishop who served as Bishop of the Maronite Diocese of Australia from 1996 to 2014, ministering to one of the largest Lebanese diaspora communities in the world. Born in Lebanon, he was ordained a Maronite priest and eventually appointed to lead the Church's mission to Lebanese emigrants in Australia.

The Lebanese community in Australia — particularly in Sydney's western suburbs — is one of the largest and most cohesive in the global Lebanese diaspora, with communities established from the late nineteenth century and dramatically expanded by the waves of refugees from Lebanon's 1975–1990 civil war. The Maronite diocese serves this community as a crucial institution maintaining Lebanese cultural identity, Arabic language, and the distinctive Maronite liturgical tradition.

Abi Karam's episcopal ministry navigated the challenges of diaspora pastoral care: maintaining connection to the Maronite tradition's Lebanese roots while serving a community increasingly integrated into Australian society; ministering to both Arabic-speaking immigrants and English-speaking Lebanese-Australian youth; and supporting the community's wellbeing through cycles of crisis in Lebanon that periodically generated new waves of refugees. His work exemplified the role of Maronite bishops as guardians of both faith and ethnic cultural identity.
